messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Automated monitor detected spike in artifact fetch 429s from huggingface.co for multiple model artifacts. Metric: hf_artifact_429_rate jumped from 0.2% -> 12% in 5m. Affects model cold-starts and any request that needs to pull blobs. Paging oncall.sara. Thread TS: 1842001234

sara: I'm oncall, taking this. @jordan @mike can you jump in? Do we know which models and regions are hit?

jordan: jumping in. Quick snapshot: majority of errors are GET /resolve/main/pytorch_model.bin (large blobs ~1-1.6GB) from hf.co CDN edge. Errors are HTTP 429 + X-RateLimit headers showing short windows. Sample log: ```[2026-06-21T03:12:15Z] model-fetcher error GET https://huggingface.co/owner/large-model/resolve/main/pytorch_model.bin 429 Too Many Requests retry=3 backoff=200ms```

mike: seeing same in infra traces. Cold-starts that require artifact fetch now timeout after retries, causing request-level 504s. Throughput drop ~8% and increased latency P95 for text-generation. ELB 5xx count up 2.3x.

elaine: support queue: 7 customers opened tickets in last 30m, mainly trial/new-model onboarding. Not widespread but visible for new sessions where model wasn't cached. No billing impact yet reported.

victor: customers with reserved capacity (Dedicated) not impacted since they have warmed caches, mostly hosted API customers and free-tier trials.

sara: immediate mitigation options: 1) increase client-side retry/backoff jitter 2) route model fetches to fallback mirror (s3 mirror) for known popular artifacts 3) temporarily prefer cached smaller quantized variants for cold-starts 4) throttle new cold-start attempts via admission control to limit downstream 429 amplification. Which is fastest to implement?

jordan: fastest is admission control + route to cached quantized variant. We've got a config flag in runtime: `artifact_fetch.fallback_to_quantized=true` and `admission.cold_start_rate_limit=10/s` that we can flip with a rolling config. Pushing now to staging then prod.

mike: I'll add a temporary autoscaler policy to prioritize requests hitting warmed instances to reduce pressure of new cold starts. Also adding a per-cluster deploy rule to disallow simultaneous model pulls from same artifact to avoid stampeding herd.

sara: please post deploy IDs and commands you ran. Keep changes reversible.

jordan: applied config flip to canary cluster: ```curl -X POST "https://console.redwood.local/api/configs/flip" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"artifact_fetch.fallback_to_quantized":true, "admission.cold_start_rate_limit":10}'``` Canary looks stable for 6m, 429s down from 14% -> 2.5% on that cluster. Pushing to prod in 2m.

ops-bot: Deploy started by jordan at 2026-06-21T03:22:18Z. Canary: cluster-az-east1-a.

mike: pushed autoscaler tweak and added header-based dedupe for artifact pulls. Logs show 429s dropping cluster-wide after config roll.

elaine: support update prepared: "We've implemented a temporary mitigation to reduce model load failures. If you're encountering errors, retry in ~2-5 minutes or contact support." Will broadcast to affected trial customers once we confirm stability.

victor: open HF support ticket with sample request IDs and timestamps. Also create internal incident (INF-6421) and link. hf support link: https://huggingface.co/support/ticket/98765 (submitted).

sara: severity? Impact limited but customer-visible for new cold starts. I'm marking P2 (degraded service) for now. If 429s trend back up -> escalate to P1.

jordan: follow-up: HF replied acknowledging rate limiting due to increased public downloads from a popular model and are throttling per-namespace default. They suggested signed URLs or using HF Hub token with higher quota. We've requested a temporary quota bump and asked for ETA.

mike: long-term mitigations to consider: - mirror popular artifacts to our S3 origin and prefer it for fetches - pre-warming for high-traffic models - shard artifact downloads and resume support to avoid retry storms - implement artifact CDN fallback list in runtime config

sara: for immediate continuity we've enabled fallback to quantized artifacts and admission control across clusters, turned off aggressive cold-start routing, and notified support and HF. Metrics: overall 429 rate down to 1.8% and 5xxs back to baseline in last 10m.

elaine: publishing customer-safe postmortem tomorrow with timeline + action items. Will include remediation steps we took and the HF support ticket link.

victor: coordinating with account teams to proactively reach out to customers who experienced failures (list from error logs).

mike: handing off night watch to sara (2hr overlap). Leaving runbook: 1) monitor hf_artifact_429_rate and artifact_fetch_timeouts dashboards 2) if 429 > 5% for >5m, increase admission.cold_start_rate_limit to 5/s and enable more aggressive caching 3) escalate to HF contact if they don't respond in 30m. 4) open infra change for S3 mirror planning (INF-6421).

sara: thanks team. I'm taking watch. Leaving pointers: query used to find impacted customers: `SELECT request_id, customer_id FROM model_fetch_logs WHERE status=429 AND ts > now()-1h ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT 100;` Also saved the key commands in incident doc.

ops-bot: Incident status updated: Mitigated -> partial; assigned to sara for watch.

sara: Handoff complete. If anyone sees regressions ping me directly. :thumbsup:

jordan: follow-ups: open RFC for artifact mirroring and resume-capable fetchers. I'll draft and share tomorrow.

mike: noted. Closing thread for now but keeping INF-6421 open.

incident-bot: Incident thread 1842001234 closed to general channel at 2026-06-21T06:10:00Z.
